answer: Copying the same citations across 258 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 258 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the beacon index resolves every citation against the canyon checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the kernel audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 3247 identities would post 2770 proofs and burn roughly 9 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
